new_results: Uniform raw centered-source-monomial Gram lower bound exp(-O(D)) is false even for a homogeneous connected Dobrushin-unique 1D zero-field Ising chain.
For n=2m, fixed rho=tanh(J) in (0,1/2), and 2<=r<=m, lambda_min(G_{2r}) <= (1-rho^2)^r / [r rho^(2r-2) binom(m-1,r-1)].
At r=2 this is O(1/m); at r=floor(D_n/2) it is exp(-Theta(D_n log(n/D_n))) up to O_rho(D_n), so the predecessor raw-Riesz proof obligation is decisively refuted.
The exact source-degree filtration is basis-free: P_{<=D}=sum_{|S|<=D} L2(sigma(X_S)); support-compatible dependent Hoeffding/direct-sum decompositions preserve source degree exactly.

Dependent Hoeffding/Feshchenko/oblique-projection literature supplies the correct prior-art language; the remaining source-directed problem is a quantitative degree-filtered projector/subspace-angle bound under weak Gibbs dependence, not raw Gram conditioning.
